text:
sam: Heads-up: BrightPath Health opened ticket #9942 asking for streaming fncall frames to their existing webhook so their dashboard can render partial structured outputs as they arrive. They
re on a Dedicated pilot and need this before their go-live in 3 weeks.

sam: Their UX team says polling every 2s is too choppy; they want incremental, well-formed JSON frames labeled partial/final and a deterministic cursor so they can stitch state.

lee: is this an API change or can we piggyback on current SSE/text stream? do they require new webhook endpoints or auth scopes?

sam: they want same webhook URL and current auth. Prefer not to introduce more endpoints. Main asks: per-frame schema (full JSON each frame), fields: call_id, seq (monotonic), event (partial|final), payload, schema_version. Also want best-effort ordering and documented retry semantics.

carmen: from runtime POV we stream token-level deltas today. To emit full-JSON frames wean assemble function-arg state server-side and emit frames at token boundaries, but that adds KV writes per call. Concern: perf and cost for high-throughput tenants.

tim: engineering constraints: ordered delivery across sharded runtime is tricky. Options: (A) best-effort per-shard ordering with per-frame seq and rely on client merge, (B) broker-based ordered relay (higher latency and infra work). Rough TE: (A) 2 sprints, (B) 5 sprints.

sam: BrightPath is willing to be beta-only on Dedicated if we gate the feature. They understand potential reordering and want idempotency guarantees to handle retries.

lee: proposal for MVP: 1) server emits full JSON frames (no partial diffs), 2) include seq and call_id, 3) add header X-Streaming-Frame: fncall_v1, 4) opt-in per-customer feature flag, 5) docs + example webhook verifier. Mark P0 for this account.

pm-bot: Note: create backlog card BRIGHT-9942 and link to ticket.

carmen: acceptance criteria from product: - Schema v1 published in docs - Beta enabled via feature flag on Dedicated - E2E test harness that replays frames to customer webhook - Idempotency model specified (we include frame_uuid and idempotency_key) - Rate limit behavior documented (bytes/sec and frames/sec).

tim: rough eng estimate if we do MVP (A): runtime changes 2 sprints (frame assembly + best-effort seq), SDK/webhook adapter 0.5 sprint, tests/docs 0.5 sprint. Total ~3 sprints but can be shortened for single-customer patch to ~4 weeks.

sam: product asks for launch checklist items: security review (no new auth), privacy review (ensure no PII leakage in partial frames), observability (per-call tracing + frame counters), rollback plan (feature-flag kill switch), and SLAs (we only guarantee best-effort ordering for beta).

lee: can we add a "frame_type":"fncall_event" wrapper and "schema_version":"v1" in the payload to make future changes easier? simple example we could document: 
```
{
  "frame_type": "fncall_event",
  "schema_version": "v1",
  "call_id": "bp-7d9f",
  "seq": 7,
  "event": "partial",
  "payload": { "result": { "items": ["...partial text..."] } },
  "frame_uuid": "f7a1-..."
}
```

sam: looks good. Product sign-off needed on idempotency and ordering wording.

pm-bot: Reminder: backlog card BRIGHT-9942 created and assigned to carmen.

carmen: action items: (1) I'll prototype server-side assembler and validate perf on a dedicated shard, (2) tim will scope broker option if ordering proves problematic, (3) lee will draft docs + sample webhook verifier, (4) sam will run the scoping call with BrightPath this week and confirm acceptance criteria.

tim: fyi we should also decide retention semantics - how long do we keep frames for replay? propose 24 hours for beta. Need product to confirm.

sam: agreed, add retention=24h to acceptance criteria for beta.

lee: I'll also add a debug flag `streaming_webhook_debug=true` customers can opt into to surface connection retries to our logs for 7d.

sam: tagging P0 for BrightPath pilot, feature-flag gated, timeline: prototype this sprint, beta deploy next sprint, pilot monitor third week. Will post scoping notes here after the call. :calendar:
